/-! ## §7. The pinned structure and the existence theorem -/

section Replacement

open TwoTerm

variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
variable {M0 M1 : Type u} [AddCommGroup M0] [Module A M0] [AddCommGroup M1] [Module A M1]

/-- **A two-term finite replacement** of the complex `d : M0 → M1`
(Mumford AV II §5 Lemma 1; EGA III 6.10.5): a two-term complex
`k : K0 → A^n` with `K0` finite projective and `A^n` finite free, together
with a quasi-isomorphism `(a0, a1) : K• → M•` whose formation commutes with
arbitrary base change: for every commutative `A`-algebra `B` the induced
maps `H⁰(K• ⊗ B) → H⁰(M• ⊗ B)` and `H¹(K• ⊗ B) → H¹(M• ⊗ B)` are bijective.

Audit (see the file docstring): `K0` finite *free* is not achievable
globally — only finite projective — and projectivity is what the consumers
(local freeness of `H⁰`, minor/Fitting loci of `k`) actually use; after
localization `K0` becomes free and `k` a matrix. -/
structure TwoTermFiniteReplacement (d : M0 →ₗ[A] M1) : Type (u + 1) where
  /-- The rank of the degree-1 finite free term `K¹ = A^n`. -/
  n : ℕ
  /-- The degree-0 term of the replacement complex. -/
  K0 : Type u
  [addCommGroup_K0 : AddCommGroup K0]
  [module_K0 : Module A K0]
  /-- The differential `K⁰ → K¹ = A^n` of the replacement complex. -/
  k : K0 →ₗ[A] (Fin n → A)
  /-- The degree-0 leg of the quasi-isomorphism `K• → M•`. -/
  a0 : K0 →ₗ[A] M0
  /-- The degree-1 leg of the quasi-isomorphism `K• → M•`. -/
  a1 : (Fin n → A) →ₗ[A] M1
  /-- `K⁰` is finitely generated. -/
  finite_K0 : Module.Finite A K0
  /-- `K⁰` is projective (finite free is impossible globally; see audit). -/
  projective_K0 : Module.Projective A K0
  /-- `(a0, a1)` is a map of complexes. -/
  comm : d ∘ₗ a0 = a1 ∘ₗ k
  /-- The `H⁰` comparison map is bijective after arbitrary base change. -/
  h0_bijective : ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B],
    Function.Bijective
      (h0Map (k.baseChange B) (d.baseChange B) (a0.baseChange B) (a1.baseChange B)
        (baseChange_square k d a0 a1 B comm))
  /-- The `H¹` comparison map is bijective after arbitrary base change. -/
  h1_bijective : ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B],
    Function.Bijective
      (h1Map (k.baseChange B) (d.baseChange B) (a0.baseChange B) (a1.baseChange B)
        (baseChange_square k d a0 a1 B comm))

attribute [instance] TwoTermFiniteReplacement.addCommGroup_K0
  TwoTermFiniteReplacement.module_K0 TwoTermFiniteReplacement.finite_K0
  TwoTermFiniteReplacement.projective_K0

/-- **Existence of the two-term finite replacement** (Mumford AV II §5
Lemma 1, two-term case).  If `A` is noetherian, `M0`, `M1` are flat, and
`H⁰ = ker d`, `H¹ = coker d` are finitely generated, then `d` admits a
two-term finite replacement in the sense of `TwoTermFiniteReplacement`. -/
theorem exists_twoTermFiniteReplacement [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Module.Flat A M0] [Module.Flat A M1] (d : M0 →ₗ[A] M1)
    (hH0 : (ker d).FG) [hH1 : Module.Finite A (M1 ⧸ range d)] :
    Nonempty (TwoTermFiniteReplacement d) := by
  classical
  -- Step 1: lift generators of `H¹ = coker d` to `a1 : A^n → M1`.
  obtain ⟨n, s, hs⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin (R := A) (M := M1 ⧸ range d)
  choose y hy using fun i => Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective (range d) (s i)
  set a1 : (Fin n → A) →ₗ[A] M1 := Fintype.linearCombination A y with ha1
  have hsurj1 : Function.Surjective ((range d).mkQ ∘ₗ a1) := by
    rw [← range_eq_top, range_comp, ha1, Fintype.range_linearCombination,
      Submodule.map_span, ← Set.range_comp]
    have hys : ((range d).mkQ ∘ y) = s := funext fun i => hy i
    rw [hys, hs]
  have hcover : ∀ z : M1, ∃ v : Fin n → A, z - a1 v ∈ range d := by
    intro z
    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hsurj1 (Submodule.Quotient.mk z)
    refine ⟨v, ?_⟩
    have hv' : Submodule.Quotient.mk (a1 v) = (Submodule.Quotient.mk z : M1 ⧸ range d) := hv
    rw [Submodule.Quotient.eq] at hv'
    rw [← neg_sub]
    exact (range d).neg_mem hv'
  -- Step 2: the surjection `g : M0 × A^n → M1` and its kernel, the fibre product.
  set g : (M0 × (Fin n → A)) →ₗ[A] M1 :=
    d ∘ₗ LinearMap.fst A M0 (Fin n → A) - a1 ∘ₗ LinearMap.snd A M0 (Fin n → A) with hgdef
  have hgapply : ∀ p : M0 × (Fin n → A), g p = d p.1 - a1 p.2 := fun p => rfl
  have hg : Function.Surjective g := by
    intro z
    obtain ⟨v, x, hx⟩ := hcover z
    refine ⟨(x, -v), ?_⟩
    rw [hgapply]
    simp only [map_neg, sub_neg_eq_add]
    rw [hx]
    abel
  set N := ker g with hNdef
  have hexact : Function.Exact N.subtype g := g.exact_subtype_ker_map
  have hι : Function.Injective N.subtype := Submodule.injective_subtype N
  set k : N →ₗ[A] (Fin n → A) := LinearMap.snd A M0 (Fin n → A) ∘ₗ N.subtype with hk
  set a0 : N →ₗ[A] M0 := LinearMap.fst A M0 (Fin n → A) ∘ₗ N.subtype with ha0
  have hcomm : d ∘ₗ a0 = a1 ∘ₗ k := by
    ext x
      obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hq
      obtain ⟨u, hu1, hu2⟩ := exists_baseChange_prod_pair B p w
      have hgu : g.baseChange B u = 0 := by
        rw [hgBC, hu1, hu2, hp, sub_self]
      obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := (hexactB u).mp hgu
      refine ⟨z, ?_⟩
      rw [hkBC, LinearMap.comp_apply, hz, hu2]
    · intro q
      obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ q
      obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := LinearMap.baseChange_surjective B hg z
      refine ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk
        (-(LinearMap.snd A M0 (Fin n → A)).baseChange B u), ?_⟩
      rw [h1Map_mk, Submodule.Quotient.eq]
      refine ⟨-(LinearMap.fst A M0 (Fin n → A)).baseChange B u, ?_⟩
      rw [map_neg, map_neg, ← hu, hgBC]
      abel

/-- **The split-off corollary on a replacement** (the B5 gate input): if
`H¹ = coker d` vanishes, i.e. `d` is surjective, then the differential `k`
of any finite replacement is surjective onto the finite free `K¹ = A^n` —
hence split by projectivity of `A^n`, so `K⁰ ≅ ker k ⊕ A^n` with `ker k`
finite projective realizing `H⁰`.  Proved by descending the `H¹` comparison
at `B = A` along `TensorProduct.lid`. -/
theorem TwoTermFiniteReplacement.k_surjective_of_surjective
    {d : M0 →ₗ[A] M1} (R : TwoTermFiniteReplacement d)
    (hd : Function.Surjective d) : Function.Surjective R.k := by
  apply surjective_of_baseChange_self
  rw [← range_eq_top, ← Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff]
  haveI h1 : Subsingleton ((A ⊗[A] M1) ⧸ range (d.baseChange A)) := by
    rw [Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff, range_eq_top]
    exact LinearMap.baseChange_surjective A hd
  exact ⟨fun a b => (R.h1_bijective A).injective (Subsingleton.elim _ _)⟩

end Replacement

end AlgebraicJacobian

open Module TensorProduct

variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {K : Type u} [AddCommGroup K] [Module A K]

namespace AlgebraicJacobian

namespace TwoTerm

/-- **Base change commutes with cokernels**, in the fibre-rank form B5 uses:
the fibre rank of `coker k` at `t` is the `κ(t)`-dimension of the cokernel of
the base-changed map.

Right-exactness of `κ(t) ⊗_A -`, packaged as a `finrank` identity.  (The
sibling project carries the same equivalence as
`LinearMap.quotRangeBaseChangeEquiv`; it is re-derived here rather than
imported, since AJC does not depend on that project.) -/
theorem fiberRank_quotRange_eq_finrank_quot_baseChange {N : Type u} [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module A N] (k : K →ₗ[A] N) (t : PrimeSpectrum A) :
    t.asIdeal.fiberRank (N ⧸ LinearMap.range k)
      = Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
          ((t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] N) ⧸
            LinearMap.range (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) := by
  have hker : LinearMap.ker ((LinearMap.range k).mkQ.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)
      = LinearMap.range (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    apply LinearMap.exact_iff.mp
    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor, LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    exact lTensor_exact _ (LinearMap.exact_map_mkQ_range k) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
  have hsurj : Function.Surjective
      ((LinearMap.range k).mkQ.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    exact LinearMap.lTensor_surjective _ (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
  exact LinearEquiv.finrank_eq
    (((Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _ hker.symm).trans
      (((LinearMap.range k).mkQ.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField).quotKerEquivOfSurjective
        hsurj)).symm)

/-- **The pointwise rank-nullity identity** for a two-term complex
`k : K → Aⁿ`, at a prime `t`:

```
dim ker (k ⊗ κ(t))  +  n  =  fiberRank K  +  fiberRank (coker k).
```

Both fibres are finite-dimensional automatically (`K` is `Module.Finite`, and
`κ(t) ⊗ Aⁿ` is `n`-dimensional), so no `finrank` here is a junk `0` — see the
module docstring on obligation (b). -/
theorem finrank_ker_baseChange_add_eq (n : ℕ) (k : K →ₗ[A] (Fin n → A))
    [Module.Finite A K] (t : PrimeSpectrum A) :
    Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
        (LinearMap.ker (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) + n
      = t.asIdeal.fiberRank K
        + t.asIdeal.fiberRank ((Fin n → A) ⧸ LinearMap.range k) := by
  have h1 : finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
        (LinearMap.range (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField))
      + finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
        (LinearMap.ker (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField))
      = finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField (t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] K) :=
    (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField).finrank_range_add_finrank_ker
  have h2 : finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
        ((t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] (Fin n → A)) ⧸
          LinearMap.range (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField))
      + finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
        (LinearMap.range (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField))
      = finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField (t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] (Fin n → A)) :=
    Submodule.finrank_quotient_add_finrank _
  have h3 : finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] (Fin n → A)) = n := by
    rw [LinearEquiv.finrank_eq (TensorProduct.piScalarRight A t.asIdeal.ResidueField
      t.asIdeal.ResidueField (Fin n))]
    simp
  have h4 : t.asIdeal.fiberRank K
      = finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField (t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] K) := rfl
  have h5 := fiberRank_quotRange_eq_finrank_quot_baseChange k t
  rw [h4, h5]
  omega

/-- **The cokernel of a two-term complex is finitely presented**, when the
degree-0 term is finite: `Aⁿ` is finitely presented and `range k` is finitely
generated. -/
instance finitePresentation_quotRange (n : ℕ) (k : K →ₗ[A] (Fin n → A))
    [Module.Finite A K] :
    Module.FinitePresentation A ((Fin n → A) ⧸ LinearMap.range k) := by
  apply Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective (Submodule.mkQ (LinearMap.range k))
    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
  rw [Submodule.ker_mkQ]
  exact Submodule.FG.of_finite

/-- **B5's engine: `dim H⁰` of a two-term complex is upper semicontinuous.**

For `k : K → Aⁿ` with `K` finitely presented and projective — the shape of
`TwoTermFiniteReplacement` — the locus where the fibrewise kernel has dimension
`TwoTermFiniteReplacement` — the locus where the fibrewise kernel has dimension
at most `e` is open in `Spec A`.

No noetherian hypothesis on `A`, no `h¹`-vanishing, and no appeal to
`rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0` (whose `hproj` would force local constancy and
so cannot serve semicontinuity — I-0884).

Proof: rank-nullity splits `dim ker` into a locally constant part
(`fiberRank K`, by `Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk` — `K` projective is
flat) and an upper-semicontinuous part (`fiberRank (coker k)`, by
`Ideal.isOpen_fiberRank_le`).  Near any `t₀` where `fiberRank K = r`, the
sublevel locus is the intersection of `{fiberRank K = r}` with
`{fiberRank (coker k) ≤ e + n − r}`. -/
theorem isOpen_finrank_ker_baseChange_le (n : ℕ) (k : K →ₗ[A] (Fin n → A))
    [Module.FinitePresentation A K] (e : ℕ) :
    IsOpen {t : PrimeSpectrum A | Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (LinearMap.ker (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ≤ e} := by
  rw [isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open]
  intro t₀ ht₀
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at ht₀
  -- The neighbourhood: both fibre ranks bounded by *their own values at `t₀`*.
  -- Openness of each is `Ideal.isOpen_fiberRank_le`; no flatness enters.
  refine ⟨_, ?_,
    (Ideal.isOpen_fiberRank_le (M := K) (t₀.asIdeal.fiberRank K)).inter
    (Ideal.isOpen_fiberRank_le (M := (Fin n → A) ⧸ LinearMap.range k)
      (t₀.asIdeal.fiberRank ((Fin n → A) ⧸ LinearMap.range k))),
    ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · rintro t ⟨hV, hW⟩
    have h := finrank_ker_baseChange_add_eq n k t
    have h₀ := finrank_ker_baseChange_add_eq n k t₀
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hV hW ⊢
    omega
  · exact Set.mem_setOf_eq ▸ le_refl _
  · exact Set.mem_setOf_eq ▸ le_refl _

/-- **Closed form**: the superlevel locus of the fibrewise kernel dimension is
closed.  The complement of `isOpen_finrank_ker_baseChange_le`; this is the
direction milestone B6 consumes. -/
theorem isClosed_le_finrank_ker_baseChange (n : ℕ) (k : K →ₗ[A] (Fin n → A))
    [Module.FinitePresentation A K] (e : ℕ) :
    IsClosed {t : PrimeSpectrum A | e + 1 ≤ Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (LinearMap.ker (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField))} := by
  have hcompl : {t : PrimeSpectrum A | e + 1 ≤ Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
        (LinearMap.ker (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField))}
      = {t : PrimeSpectrum A | Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
        (LinearMap.ker (k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ≤ e}ᶜ := by
    ext t
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_compl_iff, not_le]
    omega
  rw [hcompl]
  exact (isOpen_finrank_ker_baseChange_le n k e).isClosed_compl

end TwoTerm

      "body": "SESSION-END RE-MEASUREMENT (review-ajcr r6 close). The count moved AGAIN during one session: 23 -> 1 -> 23. Do not quote a number from this item; run the command.\n\nNOW, shared index (GIT_INDEX_FILE unset), `diff --cached --name-status HEAD` + `--shortstat`:\n  33 files changed, 96 insertions(+), 1229 DELETIONS(-)  -- 23 staged D\nALL 23 verified present BOTH at HEAD and on disk, so nothing is lost as of this writing. They include two board comments I created minutes ago, five AJC inbox items, and seven comment files across four other lanes' threads.\n\nAND THE MECHANISM THIS ITEM STILL DID NOT COVER, now filed as I-1271 and independently reproduced by ajc-p2 as I-1288: THE FRESH-INDEX DISCIPLINE BELOW IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. `read-tree HEAD` snapshots the WHOLE tree; `commit` writes the WHOLE index as a tree, not only the paths you added. So any path another lane advances between your read-tree and your commit is silently REVERTED by your commit -- as an M against a stale blob, with no D line, and with every pre-commit check passing because HEAD had not moved when you ran them. It happened to me this session on ajc-p1's galois row (3bf50581e7), restored byte-identical in 83abf6dc00.\n\nSO THE COMPLETE PROCEDURE, both halves required:\n 1. A path you did not add means you reverted it; restore from disk, which still holds their version.       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

   110	point `x : X` has an affine open neighbourhood `U` on which the restriction
   111	`M|_U` is isomorphic to the structure sheaf-as-module `𝒪_U`. This is the
   112	project-side stand-in for the missing Mathlib `IsInvertible` predicate on

   114	`IsLocallyTrivial` modules, by Stacks tag 01HK / Hartshorne II §6. Local

   120	the existence of a sheaf-of-modules isomorphism over the affine chart. -/

   123	    Nonempty (M.restrict U.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.unit (U : Scheme).ringCatSheaf)

     8	/-!
     9	# The cohomological ledger: `h⁰`, `h¹`, and the Euler characteristic `χ`
    10	
    11	For a sheaf `F` of `R`-modules on a small site, this file introduces the two numeric
    12	invariants `h⁰ F = finrank R H⁰(F)` and `h¹ F = finrank R H¹(F)` (with `Hⁱ` the `Ext`-based
    13	cohomology carrier `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`) and the truncated Euler characteristic
    14	
    15	    χ F = h⁰ F − h¹ F  (in ℤ).
    16	
    17	Nothing here is scheme-specific: the definitions and their transport along sheaf
    18	isomorphisms live at the level of an arbitrary small site with `R`-module coefficients.
    19	The Riemann–Roch lane instantiates them at the small Zariski site of a curve, where all
    20	higher cohomology vanishes and the truncation is the honest Euler characteristic.
    21	
    22	## Main declarations
    23	
    24	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv`: the `R`-linear equivalence `Hⁿ(F) ≃ₗ[R] Hⁿ(G)`
    25	  induced by a sheaf isomorphism `F ≅ G` (functoriality `HModule.map` applied to the two
    26	  legs of the isomorphism).
    27	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.h0`, `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.h1`, `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.chi`: the
    28	  ledger invariants.
    29	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.h0_congr` / `h1_congr` / `chi_congr`: invariance under sheaf
    30	  isomorphism.
    31	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.h1_eq_zero` / `chi_eq_h0`: degenerate forms when `H¹(F)`
    32	  vanishes (e.g. skyscrapers, affine schemes).
    33	
    34	The dimension counts are only meaningful when the cohomology modules are finite; no
    35	finiteness hypothesis is imposed here (`finrank` silently reads `0` on infinite-dimensional
    36	spaces), and the finiteness bookkeeping is done downstream where it can be discharged.
    37	-/
    38	
    39	set_option autoImplicit false

    41	universe u
    42	
    43	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    44	
    45	namespace CategoryTheory.Sheaf
    46	
    47	variable {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    48	  {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    49	
    50	namespace HModule
    51	
    52	variable {F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
    53	
    54	/-- **Transport of cohomology along a sheaf isomorphism.** A sheaf isomorphism `e : F ≅ G`
    55	induces an `R`-linear equivalence `Hⁿ(F) ≃ₗ[R] Hⁿ(G)` in every degree, with forward and
    56	inverse maps the functorial `HModule.map` of the two legs of `e`. -/
    57	noncomputable def mapEquiv (e : F ≅ G) (n : ℕ) : HModule F n ≃ₗ[R] HModule G n :=
    58	  { HModule.map e.hom n with
    59	    invFun := HModule.map e.inv n
    60	    left_inv := fun x => by
    61	      change HModule.map e.inv n (HModule.map e.hom n x) = x
    62	      rw [← HModule.map_comp_apply, e.hom_inv_id, HModule.map_id_apply]
    63	    right_inv := fun x => by
    64	      change HModule.map e.hom n (HModule.map e.inv n x) = x
    65	      rw [← HModule.map_comp_apply, e.inv_hom_id, HModule.map_id_apply] }
    66	
    67	@[simp]
    68	lemma mapEquiv_apply (e : F ≅ G) {n : ℕ} (x : HModule F n) :
    69	    mapEquiv e n x = HModule.map e.hom n x :=
    70	  rfl
    71	
    72	@[simp]
    73	lemma mapEquiv_symm_apply (e : F ≅ G) {n : ℕ} (y : HModule G n) :
    74	    (mapEquiv e n).symm y = HModule.map e.inv n y :=
    75	  rfl
    76	
    77	end HModule
    78	
    79	/-- `h⁰ F`: the `R`-dimension of the degree-zero cohomology of the sheaf `F` of
    80	`R`-modules (`0` when `H⁰(F)` is not finite-dimensional). -/
    81	noncomputable def h0 (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) : ℕ :=
    82	  Module.finrank R (HModule F 0)
    83	
    84	/-- `h¹ F`: the `R`-dimension of the degree-one cohomology of the sheaf `F` of
    85	`R`-modules (`0` when `H¹(F)` is not finite-dimensional). -/
    86	noncomputable def h1 (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) : ℕ :=
    87	  Module.finrank R (HModule F 1)
    88	
    89	/-- **The (truncated) Euler characteristic** `χ F = h⁰ F − h¹ F`, in `ℤ`. On a curve all
    90	higher cohomology vanishes and this is the honest Euler characteristic; in general it is
    91	the degree-`≤ 1` truncation. -/
    92	noncomputable def chi (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) : ℤ :=
    93	  (h0 F : ℤ) - (h1 F : ℤ)

    96	
    97	/-- `h⁰` is invariant under sheaf isomorphism. -/
    98	theorem h0_congr (e : F ≅ G) : h0 F = h0 G :=
    99	  (HModule.mapEquiv e 0).finrank_eq
   100	
   101	/-- `h¹` is invariant under sheaf isomorphism. -/
   102	theorem h1_congr (e : F ≅ G) : h1 F = h1 G :=
   103	  (HModule.mapEquiv e 1).finrank_eq
   104	
   105	/-- `χ` is invariant under sheaf isomorphism. -/
   106	theorem chi_congr (e : F ≅ G) : chi F = chi G := by
   107	  rw [chi, chi, h0_congr e, h1_congr e]
   108	
   109	/-- `h¹ F = 0` when the degree-one cohomology vanishes. -/
   110	theorem h1_eq_zero [Nontrivial R] (h : Subsingleton (HModule F 1)) : h1 F = 0 :=
   111	  haveI := h
   112	  Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton
   113	
   114	/-- `χ F = h⁰ F` when the degree-one cohomology vanishes. -/
   115	theorem chi_eq_h0 [Nontrivial R] (h : Subsingleton (HModule F 1)) : chi F = h0 F := by
   116	  rw [chi, h1_eq_zero h, Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero]

     9	# B5's engine: upper semicontinuity of `dim H⁰` for a two-term complex
    10	
    11	**Campaign milestone B5, the Mumford minors argument, done through cokernels.**
    12	
    13	For a two-term complex `k : K → Aⁿ` with `K` merely **finitely presented** —
    14	weaker than the shape `TwoTermFiniteReplacement` produces
    15	(`Picard/TwoTermFiniteFree.lean`:507, whose `K0` is also projective) — the
    16	locus
    17	
    18	```
    19	{t : Spec A | dim_κ(t) ker (k ⊗ κ(t)) ≤ e}
    20	```
    21	
    22	is **open**.  That is upper semicontinuity of the fibrewise `H⁰` of the
    23	complex, which is what B5 asks for once `H⁰` is presented as a kernel.
    24	
    25	## Why this route works where the prescribed one cannot
    26	
    27	`Picard/SemicontinuityH0.lean`:55-57 prescribes discharging the gate through
    28	the *rank bridge* `rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0`.  Measured in the previous
    29	round and filed as I-0884: that bridge carries `hproj`, which its own file
    30	proves load-bearing by counterexample, and finite projectivity forces the rank
    31	**locally constant** — strictly stronger than the semicontinuity wanted.  The
    32	prescription inverts the difficulty.
    33	
    34	The route below never touches that bridge.  It needs **no flatness anywhere**.
    35	Rank-nullity on each fibre reads
    36	
    37	```
    38	dim ker (k ⊗ κ)  +  n  =  dim (κ ⊗ K)  +  dim coker (k ⊗ κ)        (rank-nullity)
    39	                          ─────────────    ────────────────────
    40	                          both upper semicontinuous, by
    41	                          Ideal.isOpen_fiberRank_le (no flatness)
    42	```
    43	
    44	so near a point `t₀`, bounding *each* summand by its own value at `t₀` bounds
    45	the sum, hence bounds `dim ker`:
    46	
    47	```
    48	{dim ker ≤ e}  ⊇  {fiberRank K ≤ a}  ∩  {fiberRank (coker k) ≤ b},
    49	                  where a, b are those ranks at t₀,
    50	```
    51	
    52	an intersection of two opens containing `t₀`.  That is all the argument needs.
    53	
    54	**Projectivity of `K` is NOT required, and an earlier revision of this docstring
    55	said it was.**  The first draft proved local *constancy* of `fiberRank K` (via
    56	`Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk`, which does need `K` flat) and cut the
    57	sublevel locus as `{fiberRank K = r} ∩ {fiberRank coker ≤ e + n − r}`.  That
    58	works, but it over-buys: upper semicontinuity of both summands suffices, since
    59	only an upper bound on the sum is ever wanted.  A fresh-context review found the
    60	theorem provable with the `[Module.Projective A K]` binder deleted, and the
    61	binder is now gone.  The practical consequence is downstream: a complex fed to
    62	this engine owes finite presentation of `K` and nothing else — in particular the
    63	projectivity half of `TwoTermFiniteReplacement`'s shape is not owed.

    67	`Picard/FiberH0Comparison.lean`:38-55 records obligation (b): `Module.finrank`
    68	returns `0` in the infinite-dimensional case, on both sides, so a rank identity
